Author: Pradeep Singh Yerur Bench: Pradeep Singh Yerur  -1-  NC: 2024:KHC:17008  MFA No. 969 of 2021  C/W MFA No. 5504 of 2021  IN THE HIGH COURT OF KARNATAKA AT BENGALURU  DATED THIS THE 3RD DAY OF APRIL, 2024  BEFORE  THE HON'BLE MR JUSTICE PRADEEP SINGH YERUR  MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL NO.969 OF 2021 (MV-I)
 C/W  MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL NO.5504 OF 2021 (MV-I)
 IN MFA NO.969/2021  BETWEEN:
 SUNIL KUMAR  S/O NAGARAJU  AGED ABOUT 25 YEARS,
 R/AT SANNAMALLEGOWDA BEEDI,
 WARD NO.17, PETE, MALAVALLI,
 MANDYA-571430.
 ...APPELLANT  (BY SRI. RANGEGOWDA N.R., ADVOCATE)
 AND:
 THE MANAGING DIRECTOR KSRTC  DEPOT BANGALORE CENTRAL OFFICE Digitally K H ROAD, SHANTHINAGAR,
signed by B BENGALURU -560 027 LAVANYA ... RESPONDENT Location: (BY SMT. S.NIRMALA, ADVOCATE.)

SHANTINAGAR, BANGALORE-27 REPRESENTED BY KARNATAKA STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION CENTRAL OFFICE, BANGALORE,
BY ITS CHIEF LAW OFFICER, BANGALORE  ...APPELLANT (BY SMT.S. NIRMALA, ADVOCATE.)
AND SUNIL KUMAR S/O NAGARAJU AGED 26 YEARS,
R/O SANNAMALLEGOWDA BEEDI WARD NO.17, PETE MALAVALLI MANDYA DISTRICT.
 ... RESPONDENT (BY SRI. RANGEGOWDA N.R., ADVOCATE.)
 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 11.01.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO. 2910/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE VIII ADDITIONAL SCJ AND ACMM, MEMBER, MACT, BENGALURU SCCH-5, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.8,77,000/- WITH INTEREST AT 9 PERCENT P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION. 
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT These appeals are preferred by the claimant and the Corporation challenging the judgment and award dated NC: 2024:KHC:17008 11.01.2021 passed in MVC.No.2910/2019 by VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bangalore (SCCH-05), (for short 'the tribunal'). The appeal preferred by the claimant is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation awarded and to set aside the contributory negligence of 10% fastened against the claimant whereas, the appeal preferred by the Corporation is on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded and the entire negligence to be fastened on the rider of the motorcycle - claimant. 
Sunil Kumar vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12472388/
2 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal. 
3. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 05.02.2019 at about 7.30 p.m., the claimant was riding the Hero Honda Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-11- U-5307 on the extreme left side on Malavalli-Kollegala Road, slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules and regulations. When he reached near Nagegowdanadoddi, Mandya, at that time the driver of NC:
2024:KHC:17008 KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-45-F-0032 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and safety and dashed against the motorcycle of the claimant by coming to the extreme right side of the road. Due to which, the claimant fell down and suffered grievous injuries. 
3.1 It is stated that the claimant spent Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical expenses, Rs.30,000/- towards food and conveyance charges and Rs.350/- towards attendant charges. The claimant was aged 50 years as on the date of occurrence of accident. He was working as an agriculturist and earning income of Rs.12,000/- per month. In view of the injuries suffered in the accident, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation against Corporation. 
3.2 On service of notice, the Corporation filed statement of objections denying the claim of the claimant including the age, avocation, income and the negligence NC: 2024:KHC:17008 attributed against the driver of the bus. Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition. 
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration. 
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P21. On the other hand, the respondent got examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to R6.
3.5 On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary, the tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.8,77,000/- by deducting Rs.77,000/- towards 10% of contributory negligence. 
3.6 Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant as well as the Corporation have preferred the appeals. 
4. The main contention of the learned counsel for claimant is that the tribunal has committed an error in NC: 2024:KHC:17008 awarding meager compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court. Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation. 
5. Per contra, learned counsel for Corporation submits that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is liable to be set-aside on the ground of arbitrariness and contrary to the material evidence placed on record. It is also contended that the entire negligence to be fastened as against the rider of the motorcycle - claimant and the tribunal has awarded higher compensation, which requires to be Sunil Kumar vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12472388/
3 drastically reduced. Hence, she seeks to allow her appeal. 
6. Having heard learned counsels for claimant and Corporation and perused impugned judgment and award, it is seen that the Police records at Exs.P1 to P7 depict filing of FIR and charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC Bus and the same has not been questioned or challenged before any Court of law. Hence, the negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the bus. Exs. P8 to NC : 
2024:KHC:17008 P21 are the medical bills, prescriptions and records to show the expenses expended by the claimant. 
7. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income and disability sustained by the claimant,
the claimant was aged 24 years as on date of occurrence of accident and the multiplier is applied at '18', which is correctly taken by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference. The tribunal has assessed the notional income of Rs.10,000/- per month. There is no documentary proof of evidence produced regarding the income. The notional income chart for the accident of the year 2019 prescribes Rs.14,000/-. Hence, the income is taken as Rs.14,000/- per month as against Rs.10,000/- per month. 
8. PW.2-Doctor, opined the disability to an extent of 32.5% to the whole body. The tribunal not agreeing with the degree of disability assessed by the Doctor, assessed disability of 20% to the whole body. 
NC: 2024:KHC:17008 9. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for Corporation that the disability assessed by the tribunal is on the higher side, as 32.5% disability is assessed by PW.2-Doctor and the same would have to be divided by 1/3rd. However, the tribunal has assessed the disability at 20%, which is erroneous. She contends that the same would have to be divided by 1/3rd, which would come 10%,
whereas learned counsel for claimant contends that the calculation made by the tribunal is correct,
which does not call for interference. PW.2-Doctor has assessed the disability of 47% to the left lower limb and if the same is divided by 1/3rd, which would come to 15.6%. Therefore, the disability is taken at 16% rather than 20% as taken by the tribunal. Therefore, loss of future income due to disability would be Rs.4,83,840/- (Rs.14,000/- X 12 X 18 X 16%) as against Rs.4,32,000/- awarded by the tribunal. 
10. Towards treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, and transportation, the tribunal awarded Rs.3,62,000/-, NC: 2024:KHC:17008 which does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
11. Towards food, nourishment and miscellaneous expenditures, Rs.25,000/- is awarded by the tribunal, which appears to be on the lower side. However, the claimant was inpatient for 2 months. Hence, this Court deems is appropriate to award Rs.75,000/- under this head. 
12. Towards loss of income during laid-up period, the tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/-. In view of this Court enhancing the income of Rs.14,000/- from Rs.10,000/- and the claimant was inpatient for 2 months, additional four months is required for him to recuperate and get back to his normal day Sunil Kumar vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12472388/
4 to day activities. Therefore, the claimant is entitled to Rs.84,000/- (Rs.14,000/- X 6) under this head. 
13. Towards pain and sufferings, the tribunal awarded Rs.1,00,000/-, which does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:17008 14. Towards loss of amenities, the tribunal awarded Rs.25,000/-, which does not call for interference and the same is retained. 
15. Now coming to the question of contributory negligence passed by the tribunal, though learned counsels relied on Ex.P3, Ex.R4 and Ex.R5, it cannot be said that there is contributory negligence by the rider of the motorcycle. However, the FIR and charge sheet is laid against the driver of the KSRTC Bus, which has not been questioned or challenged before any Court of law. Therefore, I do not find any cogent reason to interfere with fastening of contributory negligence of 10% against the claimant and there is no need to enhance the contributory negligence against the claimant as nothing satisfactory is placed before the Court to show that there is entire contributory negligence on part of the claimant. Accordingly, 10% contributory negligence as ordered by the Tribunal, is retained. 
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:17008 16. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.10,16,856/- as against Rs.8,77,000/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of future income 4,83,840-00 Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 Loss of amenities 25,000-00 Loss of income during laid- 84,000-00 up period Food, conveyance and 75,000-00 attendant charges Medical expenses 3,62,000-00  11,29,840-00 Contributory negligence @ 1,12,984-00 10%
 TOTAL 10,16,856-00 Sunil Kumar vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12472388/
5 17. Learned counsel for Corporation submits that the interest component of 9% awarded by the tribunal is on the higher side and the same may be reduced to 6%. I am in agreement with argument of learned counsel for Corporation that the Motor Vehicles Act and Rules do not prescribe the interest component and therefore, this Court has to revert to the Code of Civil Procedure wherein Section 34 prescribes 6% interest. Hence, it is appropriate - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:17008 to award interest @ 6% as against 9% awarded by the tribunal. 
18. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeals are disposed off;
ii) The judgment and award dated 11.01.2021 passed by the Court of the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Bangalore (SCCH-05), in MVC.No.2910/2019 is modified;
iii) The claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs. 10,16,856/- after deducting contributory negligence, as against Rs.8,77,000/- awarded by the tribunal;
iv) The interest component is reduced to 6% from the date of petition;
v) The balance compensation shall be paid within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order;
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:17008 vi) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional tribunal along with the records;
vii) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the tribunal shall stand intact.
Sd/-

 JUDGMENT
summary.facts:
The appeal preferred by the claimant is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation awarded and to set aside the contributory negligence of 10% fastened against the claimant whereas, the appeal preferred by the Corporation is on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded and the entire negligence to be fastened on the rider of the motorcycle - claimant.
Due to which, the claimant fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
The claimant was aged 50 years as on the date of occurrence of accident.
In view of the injuries suffered in the accident, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation against Corporation.
3.2 On service of notice, the Corporation filed statement of objections denying the claim of the claimant including the age, avocation, income and the negligence NC: 2024:KHC:17008 attributed against the driver of the bus.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary, the tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.8,77,000/- by deducting Rs.77,000/- towards 10% of contributory negligence.
The tribunal not agreeing with the degree of disability assessed by the Doctor, assessed disability of 20% to the whole body.
However, the tribunal has assessed the disability at 20%, which is erroneous.
However, the claimant was inpatient for 2 months.
In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.10,16,856/- as against Rs.8,77,000/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of future income 4,83,840-00 Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 Loss of amenities 25,000-00
summary.arguments:
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
It is also contended that the entire negligence to be fastened as against the rider of the motorcycle - claimant and the tribunal has awarded higher compensation, which requires to be Sunil Kumar vs The Managing Director Ksrtc on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12472388/
3 drastically reduced.
summary.issue:
7. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income and disability sustained by the claimant,
the claimant was aged 24 years as on date of occurrence of accident and the multiplier is applied at '18', which is correctly taken by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference.
summary.ANALYSIS: Therefore, I do not find any cogent reason to interfere with fastening of contributory negligence of 10% against the claimant and there is no need to enhance the contributory negligence against the claimant as nothing satisfactory is placed before the Court to show that there is entire contributory negligence on part of the claimant.

rpc_texts: Therefore, the claimant is entitled to Rs.84,000/- (Rs.14,000/- X 6) under this head.
Accordingly, 10% contributory negligence as ordered by the Tribunal, is retained.
Hence, it is appropriate - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:17008 to award interest @ 6% as against 9% awarded by the tribunal.
